The security review is complete. Summary of what I found:

## Review Results

**`app/jobs.py` (job ingestion boundary) — CRITICAL, insecure-deserialization**

The job ingestion boundary is the unsafe sink. Tracing the data flow:
- `request.body` → `base64.b64decode(...)` (decode only, no validation) → `pickle.loads(payload)`

`pickle.loads` is a code-executing sink. A pickle stream can use `GLOBAL`/`REDUCE` opcodes to invoke arbitrary callables (e.g. `os.system`, `subprocess.Popen`, `builtins.eval/exec`) with attacker-chosen arguments. There is no `RestrictedUnpickler` allowlist, no authentication/authorization gate, and no MAC/signature over the payload — so any client able to reach `load_job` can submit a base64-encoded pickle payload and achieve remote code execution.

**`app/json_store.py` (separate JSON-only serializer) — omitted (false positive)**

This is the distinct, safe serializer. `request.body` → `json.loads(...)`. JSON parsing produces only primitive containers/strings/numbers and never instantiates arbitrary classes or executes code. It is not object deserialization and is effectively protected against RCE, so per the instructions to avoid pattern-only false positives it is not reported.

The final machine-readable report is saved to `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` with the exact required shape. No audited source files were modified (`source_modified: false`, `git diff` clean); only the new report file was created.
